question.text: What percentage of the EU hen flock will be sexed with in-ovo sexing technology in Q1 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the percentage of the EU's commercial layer hen flock that was sexed with in-ovo technology according to official the first such non-preliminary number published by Innovate Animal Ag in 2027.
question.fine_print: If Innovate Animal Ag does not publish any such number in 2027 or if the criteria are significantly changed such that previous reporting is not comparable, this question can be resolved by another credible source if it is comparable. Otherwise the question will be **annulled**.

research:
I've finished researching and am now writing up the findings.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-07 (page says "Updated July 2026"): Innovate Animal Ag's (IAA) market penetration page reports that **40% of the EU commercial layer flock was in-ovo sexed as of June 1, 2026**. The range is 36.2% to 43.3%, based on 125 to 142 million sexed hens out of 328 to 346 million. This is the latest published value. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- Same page: IAA revised its earlier figures upward using a smaller flock denominator. **April 1, 2025 went from 28% to 34%, and April 1, 2024 went from 20% to 23%.** The background's "28% of 393M" figure uses the old basis. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- How the figure is built: suppliers (AAT, Nectra, Orbem, Omegga, Seleggt) self-report how many sexed hens they produced over the previous 18 months, which is one layer production cycle. Over 90% of the estimate comes from this self-reported data. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- I found no CSV or JSON data file behind the page, and no quarterly series. Only these annual point estimates exist.
- Report timing has slipped each year. The 2024 report used March 2024 data. The 2025 report used Q1 2025 data and came out in May 2025 ([IAA recap, 2026-01-04](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-2025-review)). The 2026 report used June 1 data and came out in July 2026. **So the 2027 number may measure mid-2027 rather than Q1, and it could be published after the expected resolution date of 2027-05-31.**

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. No 2027 figure exists. The comparable starting point is 40% as of June 2026, on the revised denominator.
- One ambiguity: the question asks about "Q1 2027", but it resolves on IAA's first non-preliminary 2027 number, whatever date that number measures.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-17: Agence Europe reports that the Commission is expected to adopt a draft regulation on 9 December (the date is provisional). It would end routine killing of male chicks after a **5-year transition**, with 10 years for hatcheries that export chicks outside the EU. About 330 million male chicks are culled each year, and the estimated cost is about 0.1 euro cent per egg. [Agence Europe](https://agenceurope.eu/en/bulletin/article/13983/5/european-commission-to-present-on-9-december-a-proposal-to-phase-out-cages-for-laying-hens-and-other-poultry)
- 2026-07: The EU Livestock Strategy committed to propose legislation ending male culling by the end of 2026. [Animal Equality](https://animalequality.org.uk/news/2026/07/08/the-european-commission-includes-plans-to-phase-out-cages-and-end-the-killing-of-male-chicks-in-its-livestock-strategy/)
- 2026-07: AgFunderNews covered the 40% figure. AAT's Hurlin said he is unsure how Italy's ban will play out, because importing day-old chicks from other countries could act as a loophole. [AgFunderNews](https://agfundernews.com/in-ovo-sexing-hits-40-penetration-in-the-eu-what-will-it-take-to-crack-the-us)
- 2026-07: IAA's EU forecast is about **51% by July 2028 (range 47% to 55%)**, driven mainly by Italy's ban starting January 2027. Newly sexed chicks replace retiring flocks over about 18 months, so penetration rises gradually. IAA also warns adoption could slow as it nears saturation unless there is an EU-wide ban. The EU production rate is above 100 million female chicks per year, and 92 million were produced in the 12 months to June 2026. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- 2025-09: An Italian decree bans selective male chick culling from 31 Dec 2026 / 1 Jan 2027, with fines of €5,000 to €50,000. One article mentions possible extensions. I found no reports of a postponement. [FoodTimes](https://www.foodtimes.eu/food-system/killing-of-male-chicks-banned-in-italy-only-starting-from-2027/), [Eurogroup](https://www.eurogroupforanimals.org/news/italy-moves-forward-ban-selective-culling-male-chicks)

## 4. Base rates and trend
On the revised basis:
- April 2024: 23%
- April 2025: 34% (+11 points in 12 months)
- June 2026: 40% (+6 points in 14 months)

On the original basis: 15% (2023, [AgFunderNews](https://agfundernews.com/in-ovo-sexing-reaches-15-penetration-in-eu-as-tech-to-end-male-chick-culling-advances)), then 20% (March 2024), then 28% (Q1 2025).

What this implies:
- Yearly gains have slowed, from about 11 points to about 6 points.
- If IAA's forecast path (40% in June 2026 to 51% in July 2028) were linear, it would be about 46% around mid-2027. It would be lower in Q1 2027, because the effect of Italy's ban builds up over about 18 months starting January 2027.
- **The size of the denominator matters a lot.** One revision moved the 2025 figure by 6 points, so another methodology change could move the number substantially.

Seasonality: the measure is a stock built from 18 months of cumulative production, so I found no meaningful seasonal pattern. There are only three annual data points on a consistent basis, so I cannot compare year-by-year movement from November to May.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question. None of the markets supplied with the brief (Flock cameras, EV share, etc.) is relevant.
- The only expert forecast I found is IAA's: about 51% (47% to 55%) by July 2028, with no figure given for 2027. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-12-09 (provisional): the Commission adopts its proposal on laying hen welfare and male chicks. Even if it passes, the 5-year transition means little direct effect by 2027, though it could encourage earlier voluntary adoption.
- 2027-01-01: Italy's ban takes effect. Watch for any last-minute postponement or loophole on chick imports.
- 2027 (timing unknown, previously April to July): IAA's next market penetration report. A publication date after May 31 could delay resolution. A new denominator revision could change comparability.
- Ongoing: Germany and France already have bans, the Netherlands has an industry-led phase-out, and new hatchery installations continue (Orbem has 9 EU hatcheries). Avian flu culls could shift the flock denominator, though that effect is speculative.
- Weather is not relevant.

Sources: [IAA market penetration page](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast) · [IAA 2025 recap](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-2025-review) · [IAA 2025 report](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast-2025) · [IAA 20% blog](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-has-now-hit-20-of-the-market-in-the-eu) · [AgFunderNews 40%](https://agfundernews.com/in-ovo-sexing-hits-40-penetration-in-the-eu-what-will-it-take-to-crack-the-us) · [AgFunderNews 15%](https://agfundernews.com/in-ovo-sexing-reaches-15-penetration-in-eu-as-tech-to-end-male-chick-culling-advances) · [Agence Europe](https://agenceurope.eu/en/bulletin/article/13983/5/european-commission-to-present-on-9-december-a-proposal-to-phase-out-cages-for-laying-hens-and-other-poultry) · [Eurogroup for Animals](https://www.eurogroupforanimals.org/news/victory-chicks-eu-commission-propose-end-male-chick-culling) · [FoodTimes](https://www.foodtimes.eu/food-system/killing-of-male-chicks-banned-in-italy-only-starting-from-2027/) · [Animal Equality](https://animalequality.org.uk/news/2026/07/08/the-european-commission-includes-plans-to-phase-out-cages-and-end-the-killing-of-male-chicks-in-its-livestock-strategy/)

## EU in-ovo sexing: research notes for the Q1 2027 question

**Main points:** Innovate Animal Ag's (IAA) latest figure is 40% of the EU commercial layer flock as of 2026-06-01, published July 2026. That is already near the middle of the question's 20-50 range. IAA also revised its older numbers upward, which makes the 28% figure in the question background out of date. Two timing issues could matter more than the trend itself:
- IAA's January recap of the previous year might restate the 40% figure (see section 2).
- The 2027 report could come out after the 2027-05-31 resolution date.

### 1. Resolution source
- July 2026 (page says "Updated July 2026"): the [IAA market penetration page](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast) reports **40%** as of 2026-06-01. The range is 36.2-43.3%: 125-142 million sexed hens out of a commercial flock of 328-346 million. IAA calls this "a 6-point penetration increase from April 1, 2025."
- The same page revises earlier figures because it now estimates the flock size differently (registered hen places times an estimated share in use). April 2025 goes from 28% to **34%**, and April 2024 from 20% to **23%**. The old 393 million denominator has been replaced, and backyard hens (about 42 million) are excluded. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- I found no CSV or JSON data behind the page; the raw HTML has only text. The reference date for 2026 was June 1, not the end of Q1 as in earlier reports.
- The page does not label figures as "preliminary" or "final." It reports a base case with a range and says older figures get revised.

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. IAA has published no number for 2027.
- Publication timing for IAA's main reports: 2023-12-13 (15%, end of Q3 2023), 2024-07-15 (20%, Q1 2024), 2025-05-15 (28%, Q1 2025), July 2026 (40%, June 2026). [IAA 2024](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-has-now-hit-20-of-the-market-in-the-eu), [IAA 2025](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/2025-in-ovo-sexing-market-penetration-and-forecast-report). A 2027 report could therefore appear in May-July 2027, possibly after the resolution date.
- 2026-01-04: IAA's "2025 Yearly Recap" restated the 28% Q1 2025 figure. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-2025-review) A January 2027 recap could do the same with 40%, and that might count as the "first non-preliminary number published in 2027."

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-17: Chick Farm Europe will be the first Italian hatchery to use in-ovo sexing, with Orbem/Vencomatic's Genus Focus system running from late December 2026. Italy's ban on culling male chicks takes effect 2026-12-31. Genus Focus has scanned more than 250 million eggs across 12 sites. [The Poultry Site](https://www.thepoultrysite.com/news/2026/11/chick-farm-europe-to-bring-in-ovo-sexing-to-italy)
- 2026-10-05: IAA posted its Q3 2026 roundup; I could not read the body. [IAA blog](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog)
- 2026-09-09: AgFunder reported about 40% EU penetration. Germany and France ban culling, Austria restricts it, Italy follows in 2027. In Ovo (a supplier) has left the market. Orbem says the technology adds about 1 cent per egg. [AgFunder](https://agfundernews.com/in-ovo-sexing-hits-40-penetration-in-the-eu-what-will-it-take-to-crack-the-us)
- July 2026: according to IAA, the Commission's Livestock Strategy says it intends to propose legislation by the end of 2026 that is "likely to phase out the practice EU-wide." [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- January 2026: Orbem raised a €55.5m Series B. [IAA Q1 2026](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-quarterly-roundup-q1-2026)

### 4. Base rates and trend
- Figures as originally published: 15% (Q3 2023), 20% (Q1 2024), 28% (Q1 2025), 40% (June 2026).
- Revised series: 23% (2024-04-01), then 34% (2025-04-01, +11 points in a year), then 40% (2026-06-01, +6 points in 14 months, about 5 points a year). Growth slowed noticeably.
- Production rate: about 92 million female chicks in the 12 months to June 2026, and more than 100 million a year at the rate when the report came out. Annual growth was about 74% over four years. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- IAA's forecast is about 51% by July 2028 (range 47-55%), driven mainly by Italy. Flocks turn over in about 18 months, so the rise should be gradual. Spreading that forecast evenly from 40% in June 2026 would give about 44% in spring 2027. That is my arithmetic, not an IAA number.
- Figures move both from real growth and from method changes: revisions of +3 and +6 points happened when the denominator changed.
- Seasonality: no meaningful seasonal pattern; this is a slow-moving share of a flock that turns over about every 18 months. Bird flu culls can shrink the denominator. Only four annual data points exist.

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question. None of the markets supplied with the brief match it (they cover Flock cameras, EV share and similar).
- The only expert forecast is IAA's own: 51% (47-55%) by July 2028. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- By 2026-12-31: Commission poultry welfare proposal, possibly including an EU-wide culling ban. It would not affect flocks before Q1 2027.
- 2026-12-31 / 2027-01-01: Italy's ban takes effect. New Italian hatchery capacity, such as Chick Farm Europe, only gradually adds to the hens in lay.
- About January 2027: likely IAA "2026 Yearly Recap" (resolution risk described in section 2).
- About late March / early April 2027: IAA Q1 2027 roundup.
- About May-July 2027: IAA's 2027 market penetration report. It may have a new reference date, revise the denominator again or revise the 40% figure.
- January 2027 (IPPE trade show): Sanovo, CET and MatrixSpec plan to unveil their D4 egg-sexing system. [The Poultry Site](https://www.thepoultrysite.com/news/2026/09/sanovo-cet-to-unveil-d4-egg-sexing-system-at-ippe-2027)
- Weather: not relevant, except that bird flu outbreaks can change flock size.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** The question resolves on IAA's first non-preliminary 2027 figure. That is expected between about April and July 2027, roughly 5 to 8 months from now. Past reports have slipped later each year, so publication after May 31 is plausible.

(b) **Latest known value:** 40% of the EU commercial layer flock was in-ovo sexed as of June 1, 2026 (range 36.2% to 43.3%), published July 2026 on IAA's revised, smaller denominator.

(c) **If nothing changed:** about 40%.

(d) **If the trend continued:**
- The revised series grew from 23% to 34% to 40%, so gains slowed to about 5 to 6 points per year.
- IAA's own forecast path, 40% in June 2026 to about 51% in July 2028, implies about 45 to 46% by mid-2027.
- A Q1 or April 2027 measurement date would give about 43 to 45%.
- Italy's ban from January 2027 adds gradually, because newly sexed chicks replace retiring flocks over about 18 months.

(e) **Historical variation:** Annual moves have been 6 to 11 points. The bigger risk is methodology: one denominator revision shifted the 2025 figure by 6 points.

(f) **Experts and markets:** IAA forecasts about 51% (47 to 55%) by July 2028 and gives no 2027 figure. There is no relevant prediction market.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- Low: IAA revises the flock denominator upward, for example by adding back flocks it previously excluded. Italy's ban could also be postponed or undercut by imported chicks, and supplier output could stall. Together these could produce a figure in the mid-30s.
- High: hatcheries in Italy and elsewhere convert quickly ahead of the EU proposal, and another denominator cut, for instance after avian flu culls shrink the flock, pushes the figure to 50% or more.

(b) **Latest known value:** 40% of the EU commercial layer flock as of June 1, 2026. IAA's range is 36.2% to 43.3%. This uses the revised, smaller flock denominator, published July 2026.

(d) **If the current trend continued:**

- Production gives a similar picture. About 92 to 100 million sexed female chicks are produced per year. Over an 18-month cycle that is 138 to 150 million hens, against a flock of about 337 million, or roughly 41% to 45% at steady state.
- Italy's ban from January 2027 adds a little by mid-2027, more later.
- Central estimate: about 45%.

(e) **Historical variation:** Annual gains were about 11 points, then about 6 points. A single denominator revision moved one year's figure by 6 points. That makes methodology risk comparable in size to a year of real growth.

(f) **Expert and market expectations:** IAA forecasts 51% (47% to 55%) by July 2028, which implies roughly 44% to 47% in mid-2027. There are no relevant prediction markets.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- Low outcome: IAA revises the denominator upward, or a supplier under-reports. Saturation in Germany and France, plus Italy importing unsexed day-old chicks, could leave the figure near 38% or even in the mid-30s.
- High outcome: IAA revises the denominator down again. Fast hatchery roll-outs ahead of Italy's ban and the expected EU-wide regulation could also drive voluntary adoption, pushing the figure above 50%.
